findings.quote: The trouble with investigating fires at sites where nobody is present.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: a real strand of the text offered as the whole. Counsel cites “On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught”, “Grendisham’s objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these; it needs a probe inside a machine that later burns, and nobody has one”, and the closing “with trucks waiting and no one there to watch?” Beaten by the prompt's mainly-about delimiter: the rebuilt lede states the key’s subject outright (“the mixed-flow has a fixed reputation: the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns”) and three of five paragraphs are competing accounts of why (fines, shutdown timing, contract), which the unmanned-site problem does not cover. The repair did not strengthen this case.

findings.quote: The keepers stretched their opening hours in order to earn more of the hourly allowance.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the pay clause is stated and points this way — “the keeper was allowed threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves” — and the chandler’s thirteen-hour day (“opened at seven in the morning”, “Both shut when the evening cart went at eight”) yielded only 412 against the bookseller’s 390, so hours plainly did not track letters. Beaten because the text states no motive and one of the two keepers kept short hours (“the bookseller’s opened at two”), which the option's plural, purposive claim cannot accommodate; the surveyor’s note records nothing but “the chandler’s flap wanted a new spring”. Attractive but not complaint-grade.
